titleStmt.title: Interview with Guido Casagrande by Alan Davidson
titleStmt.author: Alan Davidson

bibl.title: Interview with Guido Casagrande by Alan Davidson
bibl.author: Alan Davidson

projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

div0.p: Transcriptionist: Jeri K. Cruse Date of Transcription: April 27, 2004

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Can I have a copy of something I said?

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Sure. Sure, we'll give you a copy.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Good morning. My name is Alan Davidson. I'm a volunteer at the Lions Hospital in Basking Ridge. And I'm talking with Guido Casagrande, who was born in 1912 and fought in World War II. He's originally from a town in Italy called Cison di Valmarino. And he is going to share some experiences with us, and we hope that you enjoy what he has to say, because he's a real good guy and he's an American hero.
Mr. Guido.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, sir.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: We're going to start out by talking about when you first went into the service and where you were at the time.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Oh. Where I was at the time.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Is this on now?

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah, it's on. It's okay. We'll let it play and we'll hear what you have to say. You were in New Jersey?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, I was in -- as a matter of fact, I was in Highland Park. That's my -- that's where I was and that's where I was recruited from.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. And that was back in 1942.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And how did you feel at the time when you were recruited?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Well, I felt a little lost, that's all. It was a loss on my part.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right. Did you have brothers and sisters that you were leaving?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah. What they were -- I don't know what to say about them, really.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Were you living with them at the time?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: They were living, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Were they in the same area of Highland Park where you were?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, they were, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-HUM.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So this must have been a big change in your life to suddenly get drafted and go have to fight for your country.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, that's right. That's right, it was a big thing. But I didn't see it that way. I saw that I was captured. (Laughter)

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You thought you were captured, huh? (Laughter)

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: That's how I felt.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: That's good. That's what we want to hear, what your real, your real thoughts were at the time.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Were you scared?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Well, not yet. I wasn't quite afraid yet.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No? And you were processed first where; here in New Jersey?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: That's where I was, Highland Park.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Highland Park, New Jersey.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And then when you were inducted into the service, what was the first thing that happened to you, and where was that? Was that also here in New Jersey?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Fort Dix maybe or ...

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: It may have been Fort Dix. That's where I went to serve my country --

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You went to Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you were processed there.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, I was.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And did you get any training while you were there?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I guess so. Not too much. No battle training or anything like that, but just marching and stuff like that.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: PT and --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, that's right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: -- and learning how to take orders.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: How'd you feel about the food? Can you remember?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Oh, it wasn't too bad. The food wasn't bad at all.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I enjoyed it.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Did you have any other people who were processed that you knew at that time, or were you just kind of alone, meeting a bunch of new, strange people?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, that's true. That's what happened, met new, strange people.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you didn't know anybody.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, not yet.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. And then can you recall the day that they said you're going over and they were going to ship you over to Europe to fight?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, we were on that ship at the time, on the boat.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-huh.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Big boat. That's when we went over.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And you left, what, out of New York?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, New York, sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. How was the trip over? Anything happen during the trip?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Not to my knowledge. I don't remember anything.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No rough seas or ...

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Boy, it's hard to go back.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: I bet it is.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: But I just don't ...

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: That's okay.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So nothing really eventful. You didn't hit any big storms and ...

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, nothing like that.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Not everybody was seasick and, you know, making life miserable?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You didn't get seasick, did you?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I didn't.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: There you go.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Nope.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. And then you landed in England.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And what are your first memories of when you landed? Can you remember any reactions that you had to the people, to the surroundings, to the food, to stories that were being told at the time?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: My memory is not great.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No, that's okay.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I can tell you that.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: That's okay. Can you remember the port that you landed in England?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No. Were there other ships there and a lot of other soldiers? Can you remember that?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Well, sure, there were, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Lots of soldiers.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And where did they put you up? Where did they billet you when you were first in England? Did they put you in tents or did they put you in quonset huts or can you remember that?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: The huts, I think.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: They put you in quonset huts.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, quonset huts.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah. Was there any additional training when you were there, or what happened when you first showed up?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Boy, you're asking me -- you're asking me some questions that --

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Well, that's okay.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: -- I can't --

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: What do you remember about those first days there in England?
Anything stick in your mind? Any incidents happen? Any men share stories with you?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Boy, I don't think I'm going to be of any help.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No, you're going to be fine. You're going to do fine, you're going to do fine. You're going to do fine. So you spent some time in England and, what, a couple of weeks or a couple of months?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I spent more than that, more than a couple of months.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: It wasn't more than a couple of months.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you were over in England for, what, three, four months before you --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Something like that, yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. Three or four months. And you were -- were you getting any training at the time, or were you just kind of passing the time?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, we were, we were marching and stuff like that every morning, and I just can't recall, but we did a lot of marching outside, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. So you were still being -- you were in the training phase.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure, sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: They were getting you ready for combat.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Do you have any recollections of the day or the time that you left England to go over to Germany? And that's where you went, I guess; you went to Germany first?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Or did you go to France first?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: France first.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You went to France?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: France first, yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And how did you get from England to France? Did you fly in or did you take a --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: A boat.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You took a boat.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you and your guys, your buddies --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: -- climbed on a boat and went over.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: All right. So what -- any recollections of France and anything that happened there? I mean you must have thought, boy, I'm getting close to --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: -- the real deal now.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: That's true, yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah. Were people starting to get more concerned about going into battle?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I think so, yes. I think so. Yep. I was one of them, too.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you were starting to get more focused --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: -- on what was ahead of you, right?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you went into France and can you recall the first battle that you were involved in or the first action that you saw?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I'm, I'm afraid I'm going to disappoint you, because my memory is not good now anymore.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: No, that's okay.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: And I can't quite remember that damn thing.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. So you stayed in France and you must have fought in France for a while.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And then you must have gone into Germany. Can you tell us about the time that you were injured and what happened on that day?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: It seems to me I was in like a basement or something, a basement -- a German basement.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: And a bomb or something came my way and it hit me on my spinal column back here.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. Did it knock you unconscious?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I guess so. I don't, I don't even remember that.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You don't.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I don't.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Do you remember the first thing after that happened? Did you like wake up in a hospital or a rear unit?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I think I did, yes. I awoke in a hospital, yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. Did you lose the ability to walk? Did people talk to you about being paralyzed?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure. I was -- that's right, exactly. I thought I was going to be paralyzed, because I was hit in my spinal column here.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. And in those first days after you were hit, were you able to move your feet and your legs?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, yes, I was.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You were. So you knew you weren't going to be paralyzed.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: That's right, exactly.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So that must have made you feel a heck of a lot better.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Better, right. Yep.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So then you spent time in the hospital recuperating?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And that hospital was in England?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: England, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And do you remember about how long you might have been in England?
Months?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I would imagine a couple of months anyhow.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Couple of months?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Two months, yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And then what they'd do? They put you on a boat and sent you home?
Or after you got fixed up, did they send you back in battle?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, they didn't.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: They didn't.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I was totally shot, you know.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah, you were disabled to the point where you could not return.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Right, that's exactly right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-huh. And then you went, you went back to -- you came back home, i guess, huh?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Oh, yes, right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Popped on a boat and came back home?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Right, right. I came home by plane, by the way.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: You came home by -- they flew you home.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, they flew me home.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. And you went back to Highland Park?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I went to Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Oh, you went back to Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Fort Dix, yeah, in a hospital.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Okay. So you went back to a hospital at Fort Dix.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And they put you in the hospital because you were still injured.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And you needed -- did you need other operations to fix you up?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I don't know. I don't remember that, to be honest with you. I don't -- I guess that's about the story, because I just don't remember.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right. When you got injured, did anybody tell you that they had informed your family that you had been wounded? Do you remember being worried about your family when you were over in Germany and worrying about mom and dad thinking that something bad had happened to you?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, well, sure we always think about that, right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right, right. So when you got home to Fort Dix, I'm sure you contacted mom and dad, right?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And they must have been real happy to hear from you.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I guess so. Okay. I can't talk for them, you know. They passed away, both of them.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right. But you can remember that they must have been real happy to --

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: -- hear your voice.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you stayed in the hospital until you got better, and I guess eventually you were able to walk?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, that's about the size of it, yes.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Did you have to use crutches or any other assists when you were fully recovered, or were you able to walk normally?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, I was able to walk normally.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So after you were discharged from the Army when you were recuperated, what did you do then? Did you work?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: That's a good question. I guess I was in the hospital, and recuperating is exactly what I was doing.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Right. And then you got better.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: And you -- did you get married? After you got out of the service, did you get married?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yes, I did.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Do you have children?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I have none of mine, no. But I do have my -- two daughters I have.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Two daughters by your wife. A previous marriage?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: A previous marriage, right.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. And where did you live with your wife?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: In Highland Park, like I said. I don't know.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: In Highland Park.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I don't really remember that.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah. Okay.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: New Brunswick or Highland Park.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Somewhere in the area here.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah. So were you -- were you living off disability checks, or did you go to work?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: (No response.)

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Well, it doesn't matter. You spent your life after the service here in New Jersey.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Um-hum.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Um-hum. And you still have family here in the area? The daughters or your wife or brothers or sisters?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Everybody passed on.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Are you the sole survivor?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: Yeah, I'm the only survivor. Sure.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: So you have no family who comes here to the hospital to, to visit you.

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: No, I had brothers then at the time.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah, yeah. How long have you been in Army or military hospitals, veterans hospitals? Long time, short time?

sp.speaker: Guido Casagrande
sp.p: I think it was a long time, but I don't remember how long, but it was a long time.

sp.speaker: Alan Davidson
sp.p: Yeah. Okay. Well, you heard it from Senor Casagrande, who is originally from Cison di Valmarino over in Italy. And I would just say as a man who does not know Guido all that well, although I played bingo with him on Tuesday night, that he is a true gentleman and a great man and a great American hero, and people like me owe him a heck of a lot. So we'll sign off now and I hope that whoever listens to this in the future knows that they're talking to a real, a real solid American.
